more_info.overview: Food-additive silicon dioxide is synthetic amorphous silica, with fumed, precipitated, gel and hydrated preparations distinguished by their production process. Its anti-caking role is to reduce the tendency of particles in a food powder to stick together. An inorganic amorphous silica made synthetically by vapour-phase hydrolysis or a wet precipitation process. Wet processes produce hydrated or water-containing forms. The specified material is supplied as white powder or granules.
more_info.uses:
Examples in the EU food-use list include certain chewing gum; dairy analogues, including beverage whiteners; vegetable oil pan spray.
The entries apply to particular food categories and may limit the amount, the preparation or the way it is used; they do not show how often the additive appears in retail products.
